To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) T cells can be raised to single residue variants of self antigens; 2) these T cells can be activated by the unmodified self peptide in a manner that requires the presence of the Fas receptor; 3) the T cells can be rendered cytolytic for self targets via the Fas/Fas-ligand pathway, but not by the perforin pathway, and 4) self peptides can be recognized by mature, peripheral T cells.
CD8+ T-cell clones specific for a variant self peptide (i.e., a single residue change from the self ligand) are tolerant to the self antigen.

CD8+ CTL specific for a single-residue variant of a self-peptide can kill Fas-positive targets in the presence of picomolar levels (i.e., physiological levels) of the self peptide via Fas/Fas-ligand-mediated cytotoxic mechanisms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms by which the immune system can distinguish between self and nonself and the mechanisms that regulate T cell activation in the periphery.
understanding the mechanisms of antigen recognition by T cells.
the regulation of CD8+ T lymphocyte activation by MHC/peptides.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the T cell population is not only tolerant to the self antigen in terms of not responding to physiological levels of MHC/peptides but is also tolerant in the sense that it does not respond to increased levels of self antigen by perforin-mediated killing.
the immune system has a very high tolerance for self antigens.
the TCR can be cross-reactive to self antigens and can respond to these antigens in a partial manner.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CD8+ TCR recognizes a peptide/MHC complex as a single unit and that the T cell response to the complex is regulated by the level of peptide bound to the MHC.
CD8+ T lymphocytes can be activated by MHC class I molecules presenting a single residue variant self peptide but not by the self peptide itself.
the TCR is able to recognize a peptide-MHC ligand in the presence or absence of a co-stimulatory signal.
The main takeaway from our work is that
T cells are able to respond to MHC/peptides that they have not been exposed to.
self peptides may be recognized by peripheral CD8+ Tcells.
the self peptide can be recognized by the CD8 T cell but that recognition is insufficient to activate the T cell.
